newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Four inmates said killed weekly in Venezuelan jails.
newsitem.headline: Four inmates said killed weekly in Venezuelan jails.

text.p: At least 206 prisoners, an average of four a week, were killed last year in Venezuela's notoriously violent and overcrowded jails, a top prison official said on Friday.

An additional 1,133 inmates were injured in fighting between themselves and with guards at the country's 32 jails, widely considered among the most dangerous in Latin America, National Prisons Director Antonio Marval told Reuters.
Among those killed last year were 25 prisoners burned at Caracas La Planta penitentiary on Oct. 22 when guards ignited a fire by lobbing tear gas canisters into a crammed cell.
Marval, citing data from a justice ministry's official report, said the prisoner death toll in 1996 was lower than the previous year's total of 239.
"We have reinforced supervision and it has meant a bit less violence," he said.
Venezuela's prisons, all crammed, squalid and decaying, hold 25,000 inmates. Only one of every four inmates has been sentenced. The rest wait, sometimes for years, to be tried.
